Feature: SII Root Complex BAR window configuration: defaults and masked write/readback
Test Description: Validate PCIe SII Root Complex BAR window configuration registers by checking reset default values and verifying masked write/readback so that only writable fields change while read-only fields retain defaults. Default check for SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL is skipped. Non-readable or non-writable registers and any addresses in the skip list are not accessed.
Meta Test Description: program.c orchestrates two phases over CNT entries defined in test_define.c: (1) chk_rst_val() validates reset defaults for each address in addr_array where read_mask_array[i] != 0 and the address is not mizar_PCIE0_SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL; (2) chk_rd_wr() iterates six data patterns {0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0x00000000, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}. For each pattern, it writes data_wr to all addresses where skip_array[i] != 1 and write_mask_array[i] != 0, then reads back only where skip_array[i] != 1 and write_mask_array[i] != 0 and read_mask_array[i] != 0. Expected value per address is computed as exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | ((write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff) & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])). Mismatches increment def_fail_cnt or wr_fail_cnt. test_case() finishes with finish(1) if any failure counts are non-zero; otherwise finish(0). A helper soft_reset_chk() saves SOFT_RST_REG_ADDRESS content, writes SOFT_RST_REG_DATA, waits, then restores the saved value and waits again; it is not invoked in the flow.
Remarks: Default check is skipped for SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL. Registers with no read access or no write access are skipped accordingly. Addresses listed in the skip list are not accessed. The soft reset helper is available but not executed in this test.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Initialize the PCIe SII Root Complex register test context and load the address, default, read-mask, write-mask, and skip arrays.
2. Check reset defaults for each readable BAR window configuration register, excluding SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL.
3. For each data pattern (FFFFFFFFh, AAAAAAAAh, 55555555h, 00000000h, A5A5A5A5h, FFFF0000h), program all writable and non-skipped registers.
4. Read back each programmed register and verify that writable fields reflect the pattern while read-only fields retain their default values per read/write masks.
5. Aggregate any mismatches from default checks and write/readback verifications and declare overall PASS only if no mismatches are detected.

- test_case():
  - Call chk_rst_val(); under DEBUG_DISPLAY prints end banner.
  - Call chk_rd_wr(); under DEBUG_DISPLAY prints end banner.
  - If (def_fail_cnt > 0 || wr_fail_cnt > 0) finish(1); else finish(0).
- chk_rst_val():
  - For (i = 0; i < CNT; i++):
    - addr = addr_array[i].
    - If (read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue (not readable).
    - If (addr_array[i] == mizar_PCIE0_SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL) continue (skip default check).
    - data_rd = read_reg(addr).
    - If (data_rd == default_value_array[i]) PASS (optional print under DEBUG_DISPLAY); else { def_fail_cnt++; print failure with addr, expected, read }.
- chk_rd_wr():
  - int chk_val[6] = {0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0x00000000, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}.
  - For (j = 0; j < 6; j++): data_wr = chk_val[j].
    - Write phase loop i = 0..CNT-1:
      - addr = addr_array[i].
      - If (skip_array[i] == 1) continue.
      - If (write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue.
      - Else write_reg(addr, data_wr) (optional print under DEBUG_DISPLAY).
    - Read/verify phase loop i = 0..CNT-1:
      - addr = addr_array[i].
      - If (skip_array[i] == 1) continue.
      - If (write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue.
      - If (read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000) continue.
      - data_rd = read_reg(addr).
      - wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff).
      - exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])).
      - If (data_rd == exp_val) PASS (optional print); else { wr_fail_cnt++; print mismatch with addr, expected, read }.
- soft_reset_chk() [not invoked]:
  - default_value = read_reg(SOFT_RST_REG_ADDRESS);
  - write_reg(SOFT_RST_REG_ADDRESS, SOFT_RST_REG_DATA);
  - wait_on(1000);
  - write_reg(SOFT_RST_REG_ADDRESS, default_value);
  - wait_on(1000);

Feature: PCIE Register Reset and R/W Mask Verification (DBI/SII/PHY)
Test Description: Verify PCIe controller registers by checking reset defaults and performing masked write/readback across DBI control, SII transmit/PHY control, and selected PHY register addresses for both controllers. Confirm that default values are 0 and that only masked/writable bits reflect programmed patterns.
Meta Test Description: The test initializes failure counters (err1, err2) and executes two phases: reset default verification (chk_rst_val) and masked read/write verification (chk_rd_wr). Arrays define target registers for each block: DBI/DBI-DSP control regs for controller 0 and 1 (rc0_ctl_addr, rc1_ctl_addr), SII transmit headers and a PHY control register per controller (sii0_addr, sii1_addr) with associated write masks (sii0_write_mask, sii1_write_mask), and three raw PHY MMIO addresses per controller (phy0_addr, phy1_addr) with default values and 13-bit write masks (phy0_write_mask, phy1_write_mask). RESET CHECK: For each DBI and SII entry, read and compare against 0x0; increment err1/err2 on mismatch. Then program SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL (both controllers) to 0x01203000. For each PHY MMIO address, read 32-bit value and select halfword based on address alignment (upper 16 bits if addr % 4 != 0, else lower 16 bits); compare against 0x0; increment on mismatch. READ/WRITE CHECK: For each data pattern in chk_val={0xFFFFFFFF,0xAAAAAAAA,0x55555555,0x00000000,0xA5A5A5A5,0xFFFF0000}: write the pattern to all DBI control regs for both controllers. For SII registers, write (pattern & per-register write_mask). Re-assert SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL (0x01203000) on both controllers, then write three PHY values from chk_val_phy={0x7BAF, 0x0001, 0x003B} masked by 0x1FFF to each PHY MMIO address list for both controllers. Verification: DBI reads must equal the exact pattern; SII reads must equal (pattern & write_mask). PHY reads: select 16-bit half as per alignment; apply per-entry 0x1FFF mask to read value and compare with (chk_val_phy[j] & 0x1FFF). On any mismatch increment err1. Test completes with finish(err2 || err1): PASS if both counters are zero, else FAIL.
Remarks: Before accessing PHY registers, set SII_PHY_RST_CONTROL to 0x01203000 for both controllers. For PHY reads, only the appropriate 16-bit half of each 32-bit location is valid based on address alignment. Validate only masked/writable bits for SII and PHY registers; read-only bits must remain unchanged.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Initialize the test and set all failure counters to zero.
2. Read DBI control and status registers for both controllers and verify they are at reset default (0x0).
3. Read SII transmit header and PHY control registers for both controllers and verify they are at reset default (0x0).
4. Program the SII PHY reset control register to 0x01203000 for both controllers to enable safe PHY access.
5. Read three PHY MMIO locations per controller, using the correct 16-bit half per address alignment, and verify reset default (0x0).
6. For each data pattern (FFFFFFFFh, AAAAAAAAh, 55555555h, 00000000h, A5A5A5A5h, FFFF0000h):
   - Write the pattern to the DBI control registers (both controllers).
   - Write the masked pattern to the SII registers (both controllers) using the documented write masks.
   - Re-assert the SII PHY reset control register to 0x01203000 for both controllers.
   - Write masked 16-bit PHY values (7BAFh, 0001h, 003Bh) to the three PHY MMIO locations per controller, honoring the 13-bit mask.
   - Read back all programmed DBI, SII, and PHY locations and confirm the expected values: full pattern for DBI, masked pattern for SII, and masked 16-bit values for PHY.
7. Declare PASS only if all default checks and all read-back verifications match expected values; otherwise declare FAIL.
